user_stories.title: Harden init container to run as non-root or minimal capabilities
acceptance_criteria: Init container uses minimal Linux capabilities (only CHOWN added, ALL others dropped)
Init container has seccompProfile defined at container level
kubectl apply --dry-run=server succeeds without PSS violations
Init container successfully creates directories with correct ownership (UID 1000:1000)
Directories have permissions 755 allowing cre user to write
Alternative approach documented: Use CRE runtime image as init container to avoid chown requirement
Production deployment passes PSS restricted validation
user_stories.notes: Current init container runs as root (runAsUser: 0) for chown operations. Two approaches: 1) Add only CHOWN capability (minimal), 2) Use CRE runtime image with UID 1000 (requires pre-created dirs in image). Decision: Use CHOWN capability for Phase 1, document alternative for Phase 3.

user_stories.title: Narrow RBAC permissions to least privilege for pods and secrets
acceptance_criteria: RBAC Role in k8s/gcp/serviceaccount.yaml modified for both production (lines 43-55) and staging (lines 78-90)
Pods resource permissions changed from 'get, list, watch' to 'get' only
Secrets resource permissions changed from 'get, list, watch' to 'get' only

EndpointSlices retains 'get, list' for service discovery

user_stories.title: Create BigQuery dataset and Log Router sink for audit log retention

Log filter includes 'cre-audit-log' log name and jsonPayload.source=cre

user_stories.title: Add CMEK support for Persistent Disk StorageClass
acceptance_criteria: terraform/gcp/modules/storage/main.tf modified to add encryptionKeyKMSKey parameter
CMEK parameter added to all storage_class_defaults (ssd, ssd_regional, balanced, standard)
New variable cmek_key_name added to variables.tf with default null
When cmek_key_name is null, StorageClass uses Google-managed encryption (backward compatible)
When cmek_key_name is set, StorageClass includes encryptionKeyKMSKey in parameters
terraform plan shows CMEK parameter in StorageClass when variable is set
terraform apply creates StorageClass with CMEK configuration
kubectl get storageclass shows CMEK key in parameters when enabled
Persistent Volume created with CMEK-enabled StorageClass uses customer-managed key
gcloud compute disks list --filter='encryptionKey:keyName' shows CMEK-encrypted disks
user_stories.notes: CMEK must be optional (default null) to maintain backward compatibility. Customers managing KMS keys must provide key resource ID format: 'projects/PROJECT/locations/LOCATION/keyRings/KEYRING/cryptoKeys/KEY'. Documentation required for key management responsibilities.

user_stories.title: Document CMEK configuration and secret rotation procedures
acceptance_criteria: New documentation file docs/gcp/SECURITY_GUIDE.md created with CMEK section
CMEK setup instructions included for Persistent Disks (kubectl + gcloud commands)
CMEK setup instructions included for Secret Manager (Terraform annotation)
KMS key creation commands documented (key ring, key, IAM grants)
KMS key rotation guidance documented (90-day recommendation, gcloud commands)
Secret Manager version rotation documented (uncomment rotation_period in secrets.tf)
Erlang cookie rotation procedure documented (manual process, downtime impact)
Shared responsibility model clearly defined (CRE vs customer)
Warning about key loss consequences (data loss, cannot decrypt)
Documentation example Terraform code for CMEK configuration
Documentation reviewed for accuracy and completeness
user_stories.notes: CMEK requires customer to manage KMS keys. Documentation is critical because key management is customer responsibility. Key loss = data loss (CRE cannot recover CMEK-encrypted data without key). Erlang cookie rotation requires cluster restart (document downtime impact).

user_stories.title: Implement container image signing with Cosign in CI/CD pipeline
acceptance_criteria: New GitHub Actions workflow .github/workflows/release.yml created for image signing
Cosign installed via sigstore/cosign-installer action
Image signing uses GitHub Actions OIDC token (no stored private key)
cosign sign command executes successfully for tagged releases
cosign verify command succeeds after signing
SBOM generated and attached to image with cosign attach sbom
SBOM generated in SPDX format using Syft
Vulnerability scan with Trivy executes as part of build
Build fails if CRITICAL vulnerabilities found
Vulnerability scan results uploaded as GitHub artifacts
GitHub Release created with signed image references
Workflow has required permissions: contents read, packages write, id-token write
Signing step executes only on tag push (v*) or manual workflow_dispatch
Multi-arch image build (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) supported
user_stories.notes: OIDC-based signing eliminates private key storage. GitHub Actions token provides identity-based signatures. Multi-arch build required for GKE multi-arch clusters. Trivy scan threshold: 0 CRITICAL, max 10 HIGH (configurable). SBOM attached to image metadata for supply chain transparency.
